title: split-stage-attn-pipeline-kv-dedup-async-commit
author: Lena Rodriguez
release_notes: Introduce split-stage attention pipeline with KV deduplication and async commit: +22% tail throughput on mixed-length workloads, p99 latency down ~12%, and KV memory footprint reduced ~35% for long-context models. Backward-compatible runtime switch; opt-in via attn.pipeline_mode.
description: Motivation: We observed a recurring tradeoff between continuous-batching efficiency and p99 latency for mixed-sequence workloads. The existing monolithic attention path either prioritized throughput (large batches) or latency (small batches) but could not achieve both without wasting KV cache or performing redundant KV writes. This PR implements a split-stage attention pipeline that separates token dispatching, kernel execution, and KV commit into clear stages connected by minimal synchronization. Key pieces: (1) a small dispatch worker that merges short requests into micro-batches while maintaining latency SLOs; (2) a lightweight kernel launcher that runs a compact 'compute-only' attention kernel optimized for tiled QK compute (no commit side-effects); (3) an asynchronous KV commit stage that deduplicates KV entries and performs batched writes to the cache with ordered guarantees. The approach reduces redundant KV writes for similar prefix requests and allows more aggressive batching without lengthening commit latency. Detailed changes and why: - Split-stage pipeline: adds runtime/attn/split_stage_orchestrator.cpp + header and a new state machine for request lifecycle. The orchestrator exposes two knobs: pipeline_mode (off|latency|throughput) and commit_window_ms; default remains backward-compatible. - Compute-only kernel: introduce runtime/attn/split_compute_kernel.cu implementing a compact tiled qk kernel that omits KV store ops and exposes a small per-thread scratch for rotary precomputation. Kernel selection logic in kernel_selector.cpp now prefers split_compute_kernel for short-to-mid sequence cases when pipeline_mode!=off. - KV deduplication: cache_manager.cpp gains a lightweight fingerprint table (small LRU with fast 64-bit hashes) to coalesce identical KV entries within the commit window; this reduces redundant memory churn for many chat-based workloads that re-emit similar prefixes. Dedup is opt-in via config and keys are stable across model versions. - Async commit: commit_worker.cpp applies commits in background worker(s) with commit-grouping and backpressure signals to the orchestrator. Worker employs single-producer multiple-consumer patterns to avoid locks on the hot path. - Continuous batching integration: the dispatcher now supports micro-batch formation while respecting per-request latency budgets; continuous_batcher.cpp got a heuristic for preferring micro-batches vs immediate dispatch. - Tests and benchmarks: added tests/benchmarks/attn_splitstage_bench.py and unit tests for dedup, correctness under race conditions, and backward-compatibility asserts. Performance: bench runs on p4d-like instance (fp16) show: - Mixed-length conversational workload: throughput +22% (tokens/s) vs main, p99 latency -12% - Long-context (8k) workloads: KV memory reduction ~35% due to dedup and delayed commit grouping - Small single-request latencies: median change <1% regression (goal met) Compatibility and safety: default behavior is conservative; pipeline_mode defaults to 'off' to avoid surprising behavior in older deployments. Migration steps are documented in docs/perf/split_stage_attn.md. Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation and selector - [x] KV dedup LRU and tests - [x] Async commit worker and backpressure API - [x] Bench harness and baseline comparisons - [x] Documentation and config knobs - [x] Internal canary on Dedicated cluster (small rollout) Related work: builds on ideas from recent continuous-batching improvements (ENG-7122) and cache eviction instrumentation (ENG-7309). There is a companion experiment branch on redwood-examples that demonstrates switching pipeline_mode at runtime. Release notes: see release_notes field. Merge notes: squashed merge; post-merge immediate canary rollout; monitoring dashboards added under Console -> Attn Split-Stage.

review_comments: Trevor Hammond (2025-11-20): Can you explain the dedup fingerprint collision risk and what happens if we get a false positive?

Lena Rodriguez (2025-11-21): We use 64-bit fingerprints with a policy of fallback full-key compare in boundary cases. Collision probability is negligible; added unit test that forces collision path via test harness and verifies correctness. Answered inline with pointer to tests/unit/test_kv_dedup.cpp

Priya Nair (2025-11-24): The async commit backpressure API looks good but ensure that the orchestrator's latency budget is not starved when commit queue is full. Please add a metric and a graceful fallback to synchronous commit for high-priority requests.
Lena Rodriguez (2025-11-25): Added metric attn.commit.queue_wait_ms and implemented synchronous fallback for requests with priority==high. See commit a11c9f0. Added tests covering fallback path.
Owen Brooks (2025-11-28): Suggest adding a flag in defaults so customers can opt into dedup only for models known to be stable across versions.
Lena Rodriguez (2025-11-28): Added config entry configs/defaults/attn_config.yaml: kv_dedup_enabled_by_default: false and documented model-stability requirements in docs/perf/split_stage_attn.md
summary: Adds a split-stage attention pipeline with compute-only kernels and async KV commit that allows safer aggressive batching, reduces redundant KV writes via deduplication, and yields measurable throughput and latency improvements for mixed workloads. Opt-in via pipeline_mode and controlled rollout enabled.
